newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria communists to hit back against capitalism.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria communists to hit back against capitalism.

text.p: Bulgaria's tiny Communist Party, in a last-ditch attempt to attract voters for the April 19 election, on Monday threatened to sue the former Socialist leadership for bringing the country to the verge of collapse.

At a news conference attended by three journalists and some 20 elderly supporters, Communist leader Vladimir Spasov said it was time to strike back against "barbarous capitalism" and bring the culprits for the crisis to justice.
"By the April 19 election we will file a suit against the renegades and traitors from the Socialist Party who are guilty for the country's unprecedented crisis," he said.
Spasov, an anti-fascist guerrilla during World War Two, said only his party could bring back the free education and healthcare and flourishing economy of the past.
"Only the Communist Party is able to stabilise the country's economy within two weeks after winning the election and to lead the people towards communist prosperity," he said.
The Bulgarian Communist Party traces its roots back to 1891 and retains its allegiance to Bulgaria's counterpart of Lenin, communist hero Georgi Dimitrov.
After the collapse of one-party rule in 1989, most former communists resurfaced in the Bulgarian Socialist Party, which won a clear majority in the 1994 general election.

The Socialists lost support as economic crisis deepened and were ousted in February after 30 days of mass street protests led by the Union of Democratic Forces, which is favourite to win the elections.
The Communists, who still use the hammer and sickle, are expected to poll well below the four percent threshold for entering parliament.
